name: Tax invoice in special cases — rule 54
definition: Rule 54 varies the invoice requirements for particular suppliers: Input Service Distributors, insurers and banking companies and financial institutions, goods transport agencies, passenger transport, and multiplex cinema tickets. Rule 46 opens 'Subject to rule 54', so rule 54 wins wherever it applies.
why_it_exists: A bank statement, a bus ticket and a cinema ticket are all tax invoices in law. Judging them against rule 46 alone would mark every one of them defective.
outputs: which rule 54 sub-rule applies, if any
which rule 46 particulars are displaced or relaxed
preconditions: the supplier falls within one of the classes named in rule 54
exceptions: an Input Service Distributor invoice or credit note carries the six particulars in rule 54(1), not the rule 46 list
an insurer, banking company or financial institution may issue a consolidated document that need not be serially numbered and need not carry the recipient's address

a goods transport agency invoice must additionally carry consignment weight, consigner and consignee names, vehicle registration number, goods details, origin and destination, and the GSTIN of the person liable to pay tax
a ticket is a tax invoice for passenger transportation, whether or not serially numbered and whether or not it carries the recipient's address
an electronic ticket for a multiplex cinema is deemed a tax invoice even without recipient details
common_mistakes: rejecting a bank charges document for having no serial number — rule 54(2) permits it
rejecting a bus or air ticket for having no recipient address — rule 54(4) permits it
applying rule 54 relaxations to an ordinary supplier
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
confidence_factors: weak when the class of supplier cannot be established from the document, because that is what selects the applicable sub-rule
weak for a document that carries none of the usual invoice markings, since rule 54 permits several such documents
validation_checks: the applicable sub-rule of rule 54 is identified before any rule 46 particular is reported missing
an Input Service Distributor document is judged against rule 54(1), not rule 46
a ticket is not reported defective for a missing recipient address
examples: a passenger air ticket carrying the airline GSTIN, fare, tax and route but no passenger address — a tax invoice under rule 54(4)
counterexamples: an ordinary trading company's unnumbered document — rule 54(2) does not reach it, so rule 46(b) still fails

evidence.quote: 54. Tax invoice in special cases.- (1)An Input Service Distributor invoice or, as the case may be, an Input Service Distributor credit note issued by an Input Service Distributor shall contain the following details:-

Where the supplier of taxable service is a goods transport agency supplying services in relation to transportation of goods by road in a goods carriage, the said supplier shall issue a tax invoice or any other document in lieu thereof, by whatever name called, containing the gross weight of the consignment, name of the consigner and the consignee, registration number of goods carriage in which the goods are transported, details of goods transported,

Where the supplier of taxable service is supplying passenger transportation service, a tax invoice shall include ticket in any form, by whatever name called, whether or not serially numbered, and whether or not containing the address of the recipient of service but containing other information as mentioned under rule 46.
The provisions of sub-rule (2) or sub-rule (4) shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to the documents issued under rule 49 or rule 50 or rule 51 or rule 52 or rule 53.
